subject: Accountancy
central_question: Which principles, concepts, systems, bases and standards make accounting information uniform, reliable and comparable?
in_scope_units: Need for a theory base and the meaning of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.
Basic accounting concepts: business entity, money measurement, going concern and accounting period.
Cost, dual aspect, revenue recognition and matching concepts.
Full disclosure, consistency, conservatism, materiality and objectivity.
Cash basis and accrual basis of accounting.
Meaning, need, benefits and limitations of accounting standards.
banned_topics: Detailed journal and ledger procedures, which belong to Recording of Transactions – I.
Trial balance and rectification techniques, which belong to Chapter 6.
Detailed financial-statement adjustments, which belong to Financial Statements – II.

known_pitfalls.claim: The owner and the business are treated as the same entity in accounting.
known_pitfalls.correction: The business entity concept treats them as separate for recording purposes.

known_pitfalls.claim: Going concern means that a business will exist forever.
known_pitfalls.correction: It assumes continuity for the foreseeable future, not literal immortality.

known_pitfalls.claim: Consistency prohibits every change in accounting policy.
known_pitfalls.correction: A justified change is allowed when it is disclosed along with its probable effect.

known_pitfalls.claim: Conservatism permits deliberate understatement of assets.
known_pitfalls.correction: It requires prudence under uncertainty, not creation of hidden profits or secret reserves.

known_pitfalls.claim: Cash basis records credit transactions when they occur.
known_pitfalls.correction: Cash basis records receipts and payments when cash changes hands; accrual basis recognises earned revenue and incurred expense.

recommended_example_progression: Use Test Your Understanding – I to identify accounting period, going concern and comparability.
Use the Shiva Enterprise plant example in section 2.2.5 to calculate historical cost of ₹50,50,000.
Use the Ram capital and credit-purchase examples in section 2.2.6 to apply dual aspect and A = L + C.
Use the March rent and advance-interest examples in section 2.2.7 to apply revenue recognition.
Use Test Your Understanding – II and the end-of-chapter questions to distinguish matching, conservatism, consistency and objectivity.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter includes Test Your Understanding – I and II, Short Answer Questions, Long Answer Questions and numerical/application questions at the end.
